newsitem.title: SWEDEN: EMU worries hurt Swedish crown, long bonds steady.
newsitem.headline: EMU worries hurt Swedish crown, long bonds steady.

text.p: Worries about France's view on the stability pact for Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) hurt the Swedish crown at midday on Tuesday but long bond yields were steady and the short end of the market firmed.
"London banks are buying marks," a trader said. "It feels somewhat shaky and it is hard to see in what direction the (currency) market will move."
"If the crown breaks through 4.5500 against the mark it could keep moving toward 4.5650," he said.
The crown was changing hands at 4.5500 against the mark, softening from 4.5300 late on Monday.
The six-month T-bill fell four basis points to 4.20 percent while the ten-year bond yields was steady at 6.99 percent.
Some dealers said EMU worries were limited on the bond market.
"Sweden is trading with Britain, Finland and Denmark where no EMU expectations are included rather than with Italy and Spain which are most sensitive to EMU jitters," a trader said.
The spread between long Swedish and German bonds narrowed to 119 basis points from 122 late on Monday.
